results.title: Medium
results.content:
I spent three weeks testing every major AI website builder I could find. Not reading feature lists or watching demo videos. Actually creating real sites, measuring real performance, documenting what worked and what broke.

Five platforms. One identical test project for each. Same business description, same requirements, same evaluation framework.

The differences were shocking.

## Why This Experiment Happened

My consulting website embarrassed me. The design looked dated. Mobile visitors saw broken layouts. Making simple content updates meant fighting through WordPress plugins I barely understood. [...] Three questions. Progress bar. Suddenly you have a website.

The efficiency was remarkable for specific use cases. Airo provides logo designs, Coming Soon pages, professional email setup suggestions, and product descriptions generated from photos. Everything integrates seamlessly with domain registration.

The setup experience is genuinely beginner-friendly, with AI assembling a ready-to-edit site complete with layout, placeholder text, and sample logo.

The problems became obvious immediately. Personalization suffers from the streamlined setup. Templates felt generic and somewhat dated. The generated design quality ranked weakest among all builders I tested.

results.title: Troubleshooting AI Website Builders: Common Problems & Fixes
results.content:
1. Be clear on what you need from a website before you sign up to an AI website builder – that way, you won’t end up with a website that doesn’t fulfil your needs.
2. Be realistic – make sure you know in advance what AI can and can’t do, otherwise, you’ll end up disappointed and frustrated.
3. Check out the functionality that potential AI website builders will offer. For example, if you know you’ll need e-commerce, will the web builder integrate with Shopify or WooCommerce? Will you have a mailing list? In which case, look for Mailchimp compatibility. There are lots of possible integrations out there, like SEMrush for SEO, Share This buttons, Google Analytics, Salesforce and Hubspot. Check which AI website builders they’ll work with before you make your final decision. [...] To make sure your website is user-friendly for ALL your visitors, use tools like free contrast checkers. Remember to add alt text to all images. And ask a website developer or accessibility specialist to review your design before you publish.

## SEO limitations

Not every AI website builder is set up to deliver great SEO. As web building gets faster and easier, you’ll need to work even harder to rank for search terms that matter. Research the AI builders that’ll do SEO the best, but bear in mind that they might not fit with your functionality needs, or your ideals for how to build your site.

## No human contact [...] This leads to a generic website that you can’t change to suit your business. And that’ll leave you stuck and frustrated. You could end up with a website that doesn’t fit the needs of your customers – now or in the future. So always look ahead to where you want your business to go, and make sure AI can build a site that will deliver.

results.title: AI Can't Make a Good Website for You. Trust Me, I Tried | PCMag
results.content:
PageCloud AI

## 1. AI Websites Have No Soul

Website builders have AI tools that let you create an online destination by typing a prompt or theme. They quickly whip up images, text, templates, and other essential site items. That sounds impressive, but the reality is far less appealing.

AI is especially disappointing on the design front because it lacks robust customization tools. This point became crystal clear as I fiddled with the website where I spotlight my books, including Video Game of the Year. I'm not a designer, but I obsessed over details like font choice and spacing. AI didn't sweat this small stuff, placing site elements anywhere in a rough approximation of the prompt. The software can't make interesting choices because it doesn't care.

PCMag logo [...] PCMag logo

Even if AI builds a foundation with potential, you'll probably have to use the web builder's other tools to clean things up. Plus, generative AI models tend to pillage from the same sources, so you risk making a cookie-cutter site.

With a human, whether it's you tweaking templates or a professional designer doing their thing, you'll get a unique website customized for your needs. Anything less, and you're doing yourself a disservice.

shopify AI

## 2. AI Content Makes No Sense

With AI, you can compromise and only have it generate some parts of your site—parts you can return to and edit later. That saves time, right? [...] There's just one problem: AI-generated content is awful. The writing is soulless and sometimes nonsensical, and the fake images are hallucinatory nightmares. When using AI to generate a site for Video Game of the Year, I got back an incoherent page full of random birds, mushrooms, guns, and only the occasional mention of Pac-Man.

Whatever you save in time, you lose exponentially more in quality. It's not just me. Google dislikes AI-generated content, too"). So, make sure that a human crafts your site content.
